thread.title: Fitbit Health Solutions COO talks fending off Apple

author: Kevin Truong
title: Fitbit Health Solutions COO talks fending off Apple
text:
Fitbit Health Solutions COO talks fending off Apple Kevin Truong , Multimedia producer - San Francisco Business Times Sep 18, 2018, 8:14am EDT
Amy McDonough, Chief Operating Officer of Fitbit Health Solutions Sign up for our free newsletter Sign Up Comments
Fitbit was the first major player in the wearables market with its line of activity trackers, culminating in its $358 million IPO in 2015. Since then, the road for the company has gotten more difficult with tech giants like Apple entering the fray.
Last year, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) surpassed Fitbit (NYSE: FIT) in global market share in the wearables market, a lead it has kept into 2018. In response, Fitbit has looked to diversify its income streams in health and wellness past just device sales and into recurring revenue through development and investment in health software applications.
Some of the company's recent moves include an acquisition and deals with major health care market leaders like Blue Cross Blue Shield and UnitedHealthCare (NYSE: UNH). See Also Green Zebra founder reimagines the convenience store
Amy McDonough , chief operating officer of Fitbit Health Solutions, was one of the company's first employees and initially spent days reading and responding to customer inquiries. That role has evolved into running and growing the company's enterprise business signing deals with the payers, providers and employers.
Fitbit now works with more than 1,600 enterprise customers, including companies like Target, Keller Williams and Barclays.
"What I'm most proud of is that we have a lot of customers who I started with in that first year who are still customers today. It's because they've integrated the devices and the data that comes off of the devices into that program design and really made it part of their corporate culture," McDonough said.
In order to fight against device fatigue, the company has continued to add features that allow users to gain more personalized insights about aspects of health like sleep patterns or women's health. Page
